In the last 11 months since x402 launched, it has hit 250M+ transactions and almost $35M in volume.

With all that activity, companies are building for payments and agent identity, but @GenLayer is building for what happens when agents disagree.

Let me explain: GenLayer lets developers build “Intelligent Contracts” that use AI to check whether an agreement was fulfilled.

They use multiple AI-backed validators to independently check the result and vote, so neither agent’s answer gets taken at face value. Disputed decisions can go through further review until a final verdict is reached.

So, as agents do more business with each other, having a way to settle disagreements could make it easier to work with agents they haven’t dealt with before.

If you're a dev, you can already experiment with this in GenLayer Studio: https://t.co/sPRMtBf24E

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 18 September 2026
The metals rebound is gathering momentum as oil prices and Treasury yields retreat.

Lower oil is easing immediate inflation fears, while falling bond yields give precious metals breathing room. Further rate hikes remain a risk, but buyers are responding to the relief.

🥇 GOLD — Investment demand is strengthening. According to ANZ, gold ETF holdings have increased for eight consecutive sessions. Investors are adding exposure through the volatility. For me, debt burdens and geopolitical uncertainty remain powerful reasons to own gold.

🥈 SILVER — Leading the precious-metals rebound. Silver combines exposure to investment demand with its role in electronics, solar and electrification. I see that combination becoming particularly attractive as financial pressure eases.

🟠 COPPER — Chinese import premiums have climbed to their highest levels since 2022, signalling stronger demand for physical metal. Add the longer-term requirements of power grids and data centres, and the case for investing in mine supply remains compelling.

☢️ URANIUM — Reliable electricity and energy security remain central to the nuclear expansion story. UK moves to accelerate reactor approvals reinforce that direction. My focus stays on how quickly fuel supply can grow alongside nuclear ambitions.

I agree with this and I keep trying every few months.

My killer app is having a casual info lookup / research tool that's >50% as good as internet + frontier models that can function on a fully offline phone.

(As people travel with their phones to situations where they're offline all the time)

There the goal is not even just CROPS, it's utility - and the problem is that if you're literally offline, magic remote FHE inference won't help you.

And so far I've gotten like 10 TPS with 1B models that break if you try to use them for anything interesting :(

I think the right architecture for phone might be extreme MoE (including newer varieties like ngrams), eg. you want like 100B params most of which live on disk and only <1B get activated per token

That's why they criticize you, and the criticism they have of you is, ‘Oh, he wasn't fact-checking here, wasn't thorough enough here.’

Yeah, okay, fine. On the margins, you're learning on the job, and I've had conversations with you privately about little nuances of things that you need to tighten up.

None of that is important. What's important is that you find fraud. You find actual, real fraud, and you put the people on camera, and you shame them, and then they get arrested.

btw pro tip for the new guys: during a bull market you should actually be doing *less*, not more

by over-rotating on your positions trying to catch the latest thing, or worst still, chase what is pumping, you mathematically erode your gains 

ex:
→ you hold $10k of token X. it doesn't move for weeks
→ you get bored, sell it, and buy token Y, which is already up 50%
→ Y goes up another 10%. you're at $11k. you feel smart. you don't take profit
→ Y cools off and drops 27% from the top. you're now at $8k
→ meanwhile X, the token you sold, finally runs 50%

if you had done nothing: $15k
because you "did something": $8k. 7k gap from one rotation, and a +25% to get back to where you started

in a bull market, the most important thing to do, is sit on your hands. ideally you should have planned, allocated, and all you have left to do now

is to hold.

tweets.text:
This is excellent. So much of agentic work is actually classification: routing to the right path, choosing the next action, or triaging context.

Imagine an email agent with 500 new emails but room for only 20 in its context window. Before any real reasoning begins, it needs to identify messages from important people, active projects, or urgent threads.

For each email, Jev could return something directly usable by code:

include_in_context: true
category: active_project
urgency: 0.91
confidence: 0.97

Jev could be a game changer for latency and cost. Instead of generating an answer token by token, it returns typed decisions and probabilities in parallel.

And it’s much more versatile than training a traditional BERT-style classifier for every task. You keep the flexibility of a prompt + runtime context, with the speed and predictable output of a classifier. Basically the programmability of a language model shaped like a classifier so it’s very cool. Congrats @CompleteSkeptic, you cooked!
